chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the people are reporting that you possess much wealth. So he said: That does not bother me.
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) passed one day by various people from Quraysh, and upon him was a torn shirt. They said: 'Ali has reached the morning with no wealth for him.'

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) heard this and ordered the one in charge of his charitable endowments to gather his dates and not send anything to anyone, and to store them. Then he said to him: Sell them to the first buyer then the next, and convert them into dirhams; then put them where you store the dates and press them in where they cannot be seen.
He said to the one who maintained the store: When I call for the dates, go up and look at the money; then strike it with your foot as if you do not intend the dirhams, until you scatter them.

Then he sent to one of those men to invite them. Then he called for the dates. When the man climbed up and was descending with the dates, he struck with his foot and the dirhams were scattered. So they said: 'What is this, O Abu al-Hasan?' He said: 'This is the wealth of the one who has no wealth.'
Then he instructed regarding that wealth and said: 'Look for the deserving ones of every household to which I used to send; look at its amount and send it to them.'

key_terms.صَدَقَتَهُ: His charitable endowment, zakah/sadaqa property held in trust
key_terms.قَمِيصٌ مُخَرَّقٌ: A torn/tattered shirt — signifying apparent poverty or asceticism
key_terms.مَا يَسُوؤُنِي: It does not harm/bother me — an expression of indifference to reputation
key_terms.مَالُ مَنْ لَا مَالَ لَهُ: The wealth of one who has no wealth — a paradoxical statement about reserved charitable funds

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali do when the Quraysh mocked him for being poor?
ai.summary: Abd al-A'la narrates that when he told Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that people were spreading rumors about his great wealth, the Imam responded with a story about Imam Ali (AS). When the Quraysh mocked Ali for wearing a torn shirt, Ali arranged for hidden dirhams to be dramatically scattered before them — silencing their mockery by revealing his concealed wealth. The story illustrates that public perception of poverty does not reflect hidden charitable endowments, and that a person of true piety distributes wealth to the needy rather than displaying it ostentatiously.
